import pandas as pd

# Read the source CSV file with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_49/training_0.csv"
df = pd.read_csv(source_path, index_col=0)

# Group by 'title' and aggregate min of 'rank_on_list' and max of 'weeks_on_list'
agg_df = df.groupby('title', as_index=False).agg(
    min_rank=('rank_on_list', 'min'),
    max_weeks_on_list=('weeks_on_list', 'max')
)

# Ensure the data types match the target schema
agg_df['title'] = agg_df['title'].astype(str)
agg_df['min_rank'] = agg_df['min_rank'].astype(int)
agg_df['max_weeks_on_list'] = agg_df['max_weeks_on_list'].astype(int)

# Write the result to the target CSV file without the index
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_49/target_multisource.csv"
agg_df.to_csv(output_path, index=False)

# Since only one source table exists, no union or join with other tables is possible.
# The failed pipeline grouped by title and aggregated min(rank_on_list) and max(weeks_on_list),
# but resulted in more rows than target (1170 vs 1162).
# The target examples show fewer rows, so likely some duplicates or slight differences in title strings.
# We should clean the title strings by stripping whitespace and uppercasing to match target format.

# Clean title strings to match target examples format
source0['title'] = source0['title'].str.strip().str.upper()

# Group by cleaned title and aggregate min rank_on_list and max weeks_on_list
result = source0.groupby('title', as_index=False).agg(
    min_rank=('rank_on_list', 'min'),
    max_weeks_on_list=('weeks_on_list', 'max')
)
